body:
The diagram below shows the stages in building a timber-frame house, from the first design drawings to the completed shell.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Building a timber-frame house
steps: Architects prepare detailed drawings of the house design
Foundations are dug and a concrete base is poured
The concrete is left to cure for several days
Timber floor joists are fixed to the concrete base
Wall frames are cut and assembled in a factory
Offcuts from the cutting process are collected for recycling
Each frame is checked and faulty frames are sent back for correction
Approved frames are transported to the site and raised into position
Wall frames are fixed to the floor and to each other
Roof trusses are lifted into place and secured
Insulation is fitted between the studs, then boards are nailed to the frame
Windows, doors and external cladding are installed to complete the shell

The diagram below shows the stages in treating household wastewater before it is returned to a river.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Treating household wastewater before it reaches a river
steps: Wastewater from homes flows through sewers to a treatment works
Screens remove large objects such as cloths and plastic
Sand and grit settle out in a grit chamber
Solids settle to the bottom of a primary tank, and fats are skimmed off
Air is pumped into an aeration tank
Bacteria break down dissolved organic matter in the aeration tank
The mixture flows into a secondary settlement tank
Some settled bacteria are pumped back to the aeration tank
Excess sludge is removed from the bottom of the tanks
Sludge is dried and used as fertiliser or burnt for energy
Treated water is disinfected using ultraviolet light
Clean water is released into the river

The diagram below shows how a solar hot water system heats water for use in a home.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: How a solar hot water system heats water in a home
steps: Sunlight strikes the solar collectors fixed to the roof
The collectors absorb heat and warm a fluid inside their pipes
A pump circulates the heated fluid to a coil in the storage tank
Heat passes from the fluid to the water stored in the tank
The cooled fluid returns to the collectors to be heated again
A controller switches off the pump when the collectors are cooler than the tank
On cloudy days a backup heater raises the water to the set temperature
Hot water is stored in the tank until it is needed
Hot water is delivered to taps and showers in the home

The maps below show a 1970s block of flats and its surroundings in 1975, and how the same site looks after regeneration in 2025.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: A block of flats and its surroundings before and after regeneration

features: A four-storey block of flats stands in the centre of the site
A car park occupies the north side of the site
A row of shops lines the main road along the south edge
A small playground lies in the north-east corner
A community hall stands on the west side, between the block of flats and the footpath
Open grass covers the east side of the site
A narrow footpath runs along the west edge to the river
The four-storey block remains in the centre, with new balconies added
The car park on the north side is replaced by a tree-lined square
The row of shops along the south edge has been extended
A new playground lies in the south-west corner, next to the shops
The community hall on the west side has been replaced by a health centre
Terraced houses now stand on the east side, where the grass used to be
A cycle path now runs along the west edge to the river
A bus stop has been added on the main road, next to the shops
